floor_history.headline: MoveImage floor 21 -> 7 and build_insns 47 -> 49 (== target): hoisting `D_8009BF28 = packed;` to be the first primitive store puts `sll $v0,$s1,16` at the head of the post-guard block, so reorg's eage

MoveImage floor 7 -> 2 (build_insns 49 == target): walking the rect argument with a post-increment pointer hoists the rect[0] read ahead of the D_8009BF28 store WITHOUT losing the H2 delay-slot steal;
Found the mechanism behind the whole floor-2 residual: p[6] is MEM_IN_STRUCT_P (expr.c:4567) so sched.c:834-839 exempts it from the D_8009BF2C symbol store and it floats 4 slots early; re-spelling it

Permuter modality SPENT on MoveImage: 4 campaigns / ~94k iterations / 2 bases / random + directed chassis, zero forms beat either base; session-3 frontier items 2 and 3 measured dead and the permuter'

frontier.hypothesis: The whole remaining residual is one unexplained alias fact: on the plain-argument base the dev-table load acquires a true memory dependence on the packet store that is absent in the floor-2 build, even though the RTL of the three insns involved is textually identical in the two dumps. Explaining that discrepancy -- not sampling more C -- is what closes the function.
frontier.mechanism: canon_rtx (sched.c:370-377) resolves a pointer pseudo to its symbol only through reg_known_value, which init_alias_analysis (sched.c:421-433) installs only for a REG_EQUAL note at reg_n_sets == 1 or a REG_EQUIV note. mv2.prio shows `insn=83 pred=75 kind=0 pred_pri=2` with final_pri=2, while mv.prio shows insn 83 with only anti/output preds and final_pri=1. Either the extra pseudo perturbs the reg_n_sets / REG_EQUAL bookkeeping, or the two dumps were taken in different scheduling passes (post-RA there are no pseudos, so no pointer is ever resolved and every pointer store aliases every symbol load).
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS modality. Re-run the two standalone dumps (tmp/grind/MoveImage/s3/mv.c and mv2.c) with BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1, separate the sched1 and sched2 sections, and read reg_n_sets and the REG_EQUAL note on the packet-pointer set insn in each. Do NOT modify the compiler -- the diagnostics are already compiled in. Session 4 has now proven that no amount of C-space sampling stumbles onto this by luck, so the explanation must come first.

frontier.hypothesis: A matched sibling that dispatches through the same g_gpu_dev_table (LoadImage / StoreImage / ClearImage) can be dumped and read for what gives ITS dev-table load its scheduler priority relative to neighbouring stores; if any matched sibling shows a dev-table load with a depth our builds cannot produce, whatever supplies that depth is the missing structure.
frontier.mechanism: The siblings are in the same TU under the same compiler invocation and are already byte-matched, so their dependence graphs are ground truth for what cc1 does with this exact dispatch shape. Session 2 killed 'copy the siblings' statement order' as a LEVER (all forms inert at 2/49), but nobody has ever read the siblings' PRIORITY GRAPH, which is a different question.
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS modality. Dump .sched/.sched2 with BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1 for LoadImage, StoreImage and ClearImage (tmp/grind/MoveImage/s3/prio.sh already does whole-file dumps of src/display.c) and tabulate the priority and predecessor list of each sibling's dev-table load and its p[N] argument load against their neighbouring stores.
